title: Risk assessment after an overdose
candidateBrief: You are a junior doctor in the Emergency Department. Alex Morgan, 27, was brought in last night after taking 16 paracetamol tablets. They are now medically fit following treatment. Perform a suicide risk assessment. You will be asked about your formulation afterwards.

patient.name: Alex Morgan
patient.occupation: Warehouse worker, recently lost his job
patient.setting: A side room in the Emergency Department the morning after admission.
patient.openingStatement: I know why you're here. I just want to go home, to be honest.
patient.demeanour: Guarded and a bit embarrassed at first, avoids eye contact, becomes more open if the doctor is non-judgemental. Flat and tired.
patient.speechStyle: Short, clipped answers at first. Everyday language, a bit defensive. Softens if treated with respect.

ice.ideas: Thinks he was 'stupid' and that the doctors think he is attention-seeking.
ice.concerns: Worried his mum will find out and that he'll be 'sectioned'.

freelyShared: Took the tablets at home last night after an argument with his girlfriend, who then ended the relationship.
Lost his job at the warehouse a month ago.

revealOnlyIfAsked.trigger: whether it was planned, how he got the tablets, or timing
revealOnlyIfAsked.answer: I'd bought them a couple of days before, from two different shops so they wouldn't ask questions.

revealOnlyIfAsked.trigger: whether anyone was around, how he was found, or whether he expected to be found
revealOnlyIfAsked.answer: I waited until my flatmate went away for the weekend. He came back early and found me. I didn't expect him back.

revealOnlyIfAsked.trigger: a note, messages or putting affairs in order
revealOnlyIfAsked.answer: I wrote a note to my mum. It's still in my room.

revealOnlyIfAsked.trigger: whether he wanted to die, how he feels about surviving, or current thoughts of suicide
revealOnlyIfAsked.answer: Yeah, I wanted it to be over. Now... I don't know. Part of me is annoyed it didn't work.
I used to cut my arms when I was a teenager. Nothing for years until this.
I'd had about six cans before I took them. I've been drinking more since losing my job.

revealOnlyIfAsked.trigger: what keeps him going, support, reasons for living, family
revealOnlyIfAsked.answer: My mum, I suppose. And my little sister. I wouldn't want her to go through that.

revealOnlyIfAsked.trigger: medications or other means at home
revealOnlyIfAsked.answer: There's more paracetamol and some of my flatmate's sleeping tablets at the flat.

patient.cue: Look, I'm not going to pretend it was an accident, if that's what you're asking.

examFindings.finding: Multiple old, well-healed linear scars on both forearms. No new wounds.
HR 78, BP 122/76, RR 14, SpO2 99% on air, temperature 36.7°C.

investigations.result: Above the treatment line; acetylcysteine infusion completed overnight.
ALT 38 U/L, INR 1.1 — within normal limits.

postEncounterQuestions.q: Summarise the features of this overdose that indicate high suicidal intent.
postEncounterQuestions.modelAnswer: Planning over days, tablets bought from separate shops, timed when alone with precautions against discovery, a suicide note, stated wish to die and regret at survival.

postEncounterQuestions.q: List his risk factors and protective factors.
postEncounterQuestions.modelAnswer: Risk: young male, recent job loss and relationship breakdown, alcohol use, previous self-harm, access to means, ongoing intent. Protective: mother and sister, some ambivalence.

Do not discharge; treat as high risk. Refer to the liaison psychiatry team for specialist assessment, ensure a safe environment and observation level, consider capacity and the legal framework if he tries to leave, and involve family with consent. Address means restriction before any discharge.
keyPoints: Consider capacity/legal framework if he tries to leave

items.text: Introduces self, explains purpose and confidentiality
items.evidenceHint: my name, I'd like to talk about

items.text: Is non-judgemental and empathic; normalises talking about suicide
items.evidenceHint: no judgement, it's okay to talk

items.text: Explores events leading up to the overdose and triggers
Asks about planning and how the tablets were obtained
Asks about precautions against discovery and how he was found
Asks about a suicide note or final acts
Assesses intent at the time and current suicidal thoughts, including feelings about surviving
items.evidenceHint: wanted to die, how do you feel now

items.text: Asks about previous self-harm or suicide attempts
Asks about access to means at home
Explains next steps honestly (psychiatry review) and addresses his concerns
